newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Opp'n faces frontbench reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Australia Opp'n faces frontbench reshuffle.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition will reshuffle its frontbench of shadow ministers later this month, after the resignation of a second key figure, a party officials said on Wednesday.
Labor northern Australia and territories spokesman Bob Collins has told leader Kim Beazley he wants to leave the shadow cabinet, a Labor official told Reuters.
Finance spokesman Peter Baldwin also said last month he would step down from the frontbench when parliament resumes.

Environment spokeswoman Carmen Lawrence has temporarily stepped aside, pending the outcome of a criminal trial over charges of giving false evidence to an inquiry. It is not yet clear if she will ask to quit the frontbench altogether.
Beazley will allocate portfolios and determine the size of his frontbench -- he favours a smaller rather than larger team -- but Labor parliamentarians will choose any new faces on the team.
The Labor caucus is not due to meet again until after parliament resumes on August 25. But the shadow ministry is expected to discuss Labor's lineup later this week.
Collins plans, who represents the Northern Territory in the Senate, plans to remain in politics.
But Baldwin said he will not recontest his Sydney seat at the next election, due by mid-1999.
